Request for Proposal (RFP) - Feature Expansion for Rental Platform (Golang/Flutter)

Overview
We are looking to commission a series of feature enhancements for our existing peer-to-peer rental platform. We are seeking a detailed technical proposal and cost estimate for the scope of work outlined below.
Current Architecture & Tech Stack
Any proposed work must integrate seamlessly with our existing infrastructure.
 * Backend: Golang (using Fiber framework).
 * Database: MongoDB (Client-Hosted) utilizing MongoDB Atlas Triggers for automation.
 * Mobile App: Flutter (iOS & Android).
 * Infrastructure: AWS App Runner (Dockerized), Amazon ECR, Amazon S3.
 * CI/CD: Azure DevOps (Repos & Pipelines).
 * 3rd Party Services: Stripe (Payments), GetStream.io (Chat), Firebase (FCM), Zepto Mail.
Scope of Work
We require the following enhancements to be scoped and priced. Please provide line-item estimates for the following modules:
1. Payment & Financial Automation
 * Payment Automation: Automate the release of funds from borrower to lender upon successful transaction completion. This requires updating our Stripe integration to handle automated payouts based on transaction status logic.
 * Tia Protect (Insurance Integration): Enable an optional "add-on" insurance product during the checkout flow. This involves backend logic to calculate the additional fee and route this specific revenue stream correctly within Stripe.
2. Geolocation & Logistics
 * Geolocation Search: Implement a radius-based search allowing users to find items within a specific distance. This will require implementing geospatial indexing and queries in our existing MongoDB instance.
 * Drop & Collect: Logic to detect if a borrower and lender are within a defined radius. If satisfied, the system must prompt the user to select "Drop & Collect," automatically removing the shipping cost from the transaction total.
3. Rental Logic Enhancements
 * Try-On Functionality: Create a new rental tier allowing users to request items for a "Try-on" period (e.g., 24 hours) at a fractional cost. This requires enforcing strict time limits via backend schedulers (utilizing our existing MongoDB Triggers setup).
 * User Profile Enhancements: Expand public profiles to display user rental history, "most viewed" items (requiring a view-counter implementation), and a list of favorited items.
4. Web & Admin Expansion
 * Web-App Database Integration: We require website browsing and transaction functionality that mirrors the mobile app. The web frontend must connect to the same Golang backend and MongoDB database to ensure real-time synchronization between web and mobile users.
 * Admin Panel Upgrade:
   * Integrate chat functionality into the Admin Panel to allow support staff to message users directly (leveraging our existing GetStream.io infrastructure).
   * Add dashboard widgets for tracking KPIs: active rentals, total revenue, and user metrics.
5. Notification System
 * Smart Notifications: Enhancement of the notification center to allow individual clearing of alerts.
 * Deep Linking: Implement "click-through" functionality where tapping a push notification routes the user to the specific screen (e.g., specific Order ID) within the Flutter app.
Deliverables & Deployment
 * Code Quality: All backend code must be written in Golang and follow our existing repository structure in Azure DevOps.
 * Deployment: Features must be compatible with our zero-downtime deployment flow via AWS App Runner.
 * Security: Secrets must continue to be managed via Azure Secure Variables and AWS App Runner environment variables.
Proposal Requirements
Please provide a quote that includes:
 * Cost Breakdown: Estimated cost per module listed above.
 * Timeline: Estimated weeks/months for completion.
 * Approach: Brief summary of how you intend to handle the database synchronization for the web integration.
Thank you. We look forward to your response.

Description:
Hi,
I am looking for a quote to build ad develop an application for Android and IOS.
In a nutshell it is a booking system to allow members of a club to book an asset (boat) for a pre-defined period of time (slot).
The club in question will be a subscription based model for boats, ie: instead of buying a boat, members can pay a fee to access a fleet of boats with some limitations. 

The assets are boats and initially there will be 3-5 of these with 4-5 members per boat, total up to 25 members.
The member will be provided a login by the administrator, they will not be able to sign-up themselves.
Members:
Each member should be able to book a "slot" by either selecting a date on the calendar to see what boats are available or by selecting a specific boat to see what "slots" that boat is available.
When they select a boat, there should be information available on this boat before they choose to book. 
The member can "check out" a boat when they take it and "check in" a boat upon return. There should be a view for them to see their history.
There should be a way to report an issue with a boat - a form perhaps that can take a photo. This will be sent to the admins.
The member should also be able to see a "news / updates" page, updated by admins and
The admin should be able to add/edit/remove both boats and members. 
The admin can also edit "slot times" - seasonality and be able to remove access to certain boats from certain members as required operationally.
Members should also be able to be put into "groups" to allow access to certain boats only. They should only be able to see the boats in the group in which they are active.
Admins should be able to limit the amount of active bookings a member can have (likely 3/4 by default)
The administration should be able to be managed from a dashboard outside the apps.

That's the concept in a nutshell, overall it's relatively simple and if successful, more features would be added in the future as well as expanding locations and membership numbers.
Please let me know if you require any further information prior to quoting.

Kind regards,
Gregor McGuckin

What Tora is
Tora is a website where Irish startups can book experienced HR, Operations, or strategic leadership professionals for just 1‑3 days each week. Think of it as Airbnb, but for short‑term senior talent instead of holiday homes.

How Tora works (step‑by‑step)

Professionals (Contractors) join the site

They fill in a profile and click a “Connect with Stripe” button so they can get paid.

Startups (Clients) post a short brief

They say which role they need, how many days per week, and for how many weeks.

Me (or an admin dashboard) suggest 3‑5 matching professionals

The client chooses one.

Both sides sign a simple day‑rate contract online

An e‑signature tool pops up, they sign, and a PDF copy is stored.

The client pays up‑front for the booked days

Stripe automatically splits the money: 90 % to the professional, 10 % to me (the platform).

The professional blocks the agreed days on a calendar

After a day is worked they click “Mark complete.”

Stripe releases the money and emails an invoice

The client receives a VAT‑compliant invoice; the professional sees the payout.

Both sides can rate the experience; we keep the 10 % fee

Repeat.

Everything above can run with a very small first version (MVP): basic profiles, a form for briefs, a simple admin page to match people, Stripe for payments, and DocuSign/HelloSign for signatures.

It will involve the production of an API which must be able to integrate with other separate systems. Our API will extract data from these systems and store them on a cloudbase, AWS I suspect will be the cloud base we will store on however your expertise may suggest an alternative cloud storage solution. 
The data extracted from these systems which the API will then send to the cloud will be simple singular files, data which is in most cases ready to be transferred as is. 
Our API will need to be able to integrate with multiple different systems, all the exact same in characteristics and functionality however different protocols and authentication tokens will be necessary to integrate with each particular system. In short they are the same type of systems that the API you develop will integrate with, however each different system will use different protocols and integration will be slightly different with each system. 
Our users will need instant access to the data stored on the cloud. 
This software system which you will be creating contains a physical activation to initiate steps and hardware will be involved in the form of scanners. 
Data stored on cloud will need to be accessed via mobile app and web browser.

Description:
Hi,

I am hoping to build order shipping software/platform like Eshopworld or Shipstation. I am making exploratory investigations into how much this is going to cost and don't know exactly everything that is needed to build such a platform. I do know I will need integrate logistics carriers API's into my platform for shipping times and rates and am hoping to using World Options for this although I am open to using other firms. 

I will also need to build in a payments side (exchange rates, customs, excise, VAT calculations, shipping, percentage to be taken by my company out of each transaction) of the platform and am hoping to use Stripe to do this however I am open to learning if this is the best option and if it can be done without their help. 

I would prefer if you contacted me via email and discussed if it would be possible to build such software and give a rough estimate on how much this might cost in total. If I decide to go with your company we can then discuss the ins and outs and details of building the platform.

Project Background:
I wanted to ship Gap clothes to Ireland from America and they didn’t ship here. Nautica, Dockers and other brands ship to some countries but not all countries and that includes Ireland. I reflected on this to see if this was a problem I could solve and started down this road. I did research and came across an Irish (I am Irish) order shipping software company. Of course, I recognised this company as they do the order shipping software for one of my favourite American brands J-Crew. The name of the company is eShopWorld. I am still putting all the pieces together and learning as I go and I still do not have a full idea of all the pieces required for my software/platform but I have a few calls set up for the new year when someone who is in this exact business will walk me through what is required to build such a software.
The Problem:
The problem I identified is that there are many e-commerce marketplaces and sellers who do not ship to certain countries.
The Solution:
I aim to solve this problem by providing a plug and play e-commerce platform/software to individual vendor businesses that will enable them to ship internationally and to otherwise unreachable countries. It will be code inserted on top of vendor website code and will manage and complete everything related to orders and delivery.
Platforms: 
Web initially but as it’s a plug and play software that inserts on top of the vendor websites code, it will be mainly for website vendors.
Main set of features/Functionality:
Four main products - starter, basic, intermediate & advanced for different quantities of orders the vendor websites/clients will be receiving and fulfilling. Some of the subject areas around order shipping include add-on advanced features for the software: compliance, data analytics, fraud protection, risk management, supplier relationship management and demand generation.
Furthermore, the software will include the following services: Import orders from 100+ selling channels, marketplaces, Enterprise Resource Planning, Customer Relationship Management, or Inventory Management Software which includes the ability to do scan-based workflows, bulk updates, and automation processes to quickly fulfil the day’s shipments.
Functionalities: 
Payments - everything payments related - so hoping to work with Stripe for this part if your firm doesn’t deal with payments. This will include calculating exchange rates on orders, customs, excise, VAT, shipping rates and selling price for the goods in question. 
Order fulfilment: Once the payment is made the order has to be fulfilled. This requires physical packaging of the goods and collection by logistics carrier. It will entail a system which will track and trace every order from payment to delivery.
Logistics - for this we will be using a logistics carrier company like World Options (these are firms that have multiple logistics companies like FedEx and DHL in their offerings so that goods can be booked on shipments and moved) and plugging their APIs into our software so that shipping times & rates will be calculated when taking and receiving the order.
Seller channels - What online marketplace my e-commerce prospects sell on e.g. seller fulfilled Prime, EBay etc. This I have to find out about from the person I have the call with a person who is in this exact business. In short, he will tell me how to advertise or plug-in the platform to sellers on marketplaces like Amazon 
Warehouse/Inventory Management. For more advanced users who have large companies or brands shipping large quantities of goods in short space of time. Establish efficient storage and digital inventory management systems. Inventory Management Systems (IMS) are digital tools that enable real-time tracking and management of inventory. Key components often include barcoding systems, RFID technology, software platforms, and analytics. Most of the customers have their own fulfilment operation but they advertise on Amazon and fulfil directly. They help sellers reach different market places. As I’m unsure whether the carrier logistics firms carry out this side of the business, I am unsure if this will be required.
Features/Functionality:
Client User Interface:
Order Management: This will include an interactive interface where clients can manage and edit orders. Details on functionalities and dropdown choices for each order. Create New Order, View Orders, Edit Order, Cancel Order, Order Status, Order History, Shipping Information, Invoice/Receipt, Returns and Refunds, Payment Information, Customer Communication, Fulfillment Details, Batch Processing, Export Orders, Archive Orders, Settings and Configuration, Help and Support:
Shipping Management: This will include interactive interface where clients can manage and edit shipping arrangements. Details on functionalities and dropdown choices for each order. supply chain visibility and tracking. The wealth of data collected through IoT sensors, RFID, and GPS tracking can be analysed to identify trends and areas for improvement in the supply chain. This data-driven approach can lead to more efficient operations and cost savings
Inventory Management: This will include interactive interface where clients can manage and edit their own inventory. Details on functionalities and dropdown choices for each order. Inventory Management Systems (IMS) are digital tools that enable real-time tracking and management of inventory. Key components often include barcoding systems, RFID technology, software platforms, and analytics. The benefits for clients include efficient order fulfilment. Clients benefit from rapid, accurate, and efficient order processing, ensuring that products are shipped promptly and accurately. Clients have real-time visibility into their inventory levels, helping them avoid overstocking or stockouts, and make informed decisions about restocking.
Returns Management: To structure a fee that covers returns of goods in an e-commerce business, you can implement a returns policy that includes the following elements: 1.) Return Window: Define a specific period within which customers can request returns, such as 30 days from the date of purchase. 2.) Return Eligibility: Clearly outline the conditions under which returns are accepted. This may include criteria such as unused or unopened items, original packaging, and proof of purchase. 3.) Return Authorization: Require customers to request authorization for returns through your website or customer support channels. This allows you to track and approve returns. 4.) Return Shipping: Specify who is responsible for return shipping costs. Options include: Free returns: The e-commerce business covers return shipping costs. Customer-paid returns: Customers are responsible for return shipping fees. Split returns: Both the business and the customer share the return shipping costs. 5.) Restocking Fees: Consider implementing a restocking fee for returns to cover handling and processing expenses. This fee can be a fixed amount or a percentage of the item's purchase price. 6.) Refund Methods: Clearly communicate how refunds will be processed. Options include: Full refund to the original payment method. Store credit or gift card for future purchases. Exchange for a different product. 7.) Return Process: Provide step-by-step instructions for customers on how to initiate a return, including where to send the item and any required documentation. 8.) Return Tracking: Implement a system to track returns and refunds to ensure a smooth process and prevent fraud. 9.) Transparency: Make your return policy easy to find on your website and ensure it's written in clear, understandable language. 10.) Customer Support: Offer responsive customer support to assist customers with return inquiries and provide timely updates on the status of their returns.
Compliance, Data Security, Fraud Protection – 1.) Regulatory Compliance: Overview of compliance standards and certifications achieved by the platform, such as GDPR, PCI DSS, HIPAA, etc. Access to compliance documentation and reports for auditing purposes. 2.) Data Encryption: Option to enable encryption for data in transit and at rest to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access. Choice of encryption algorithms and key management. 3.) User Access Control: User role management to assign specific access privileges based on job roles and responsibilities. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) for an added layer of user security. 4.) Data Privacy Settings: Configuration options for data privacy settings, allowing clients to define data retention policies and consent management.5.) Audit Logs: Access to detailed logs of user activities, data access, and system events for compliance auditing. Ability to search and filter audit logs for specific events or time periods. 6.) Compliance Reporting: Generation of compliance reports that clients can use for internal and external audits or regulatory submissions. 7.) Data Masking and Redaction: Features to mask or redact sensitive data in user interfaces, reports, or exports to maintain data privacy. 8.) Secure File Upload/Download: Secure methods for clients to upload and download sensitive documents or data files. Scanning and malware detection for uploaded files. 9.) Fraud Detection and Prevention: Real-time monitoring for suspicious activities and transactions. Integration with fraud detection algorithms and third-party services. 10.)
